sources.title: 3W Dataset 2.0.0: real-data imperfections
sources.section: Background & Summary, paragraphs on real instances
sources.attribution: Vaz Vargas, R. E., de Melo Junior, A. J., de Campos Lima, C. B. et al., Scientific Data 13, 949 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-07225-z.
sources.content: The 3W publication describes real industrial records that retain missing variables, frozen variables and outliers. Missing observations in a particular window therefore require explicit handling; this general dataset description does not establish the cause of any individual missing reading.

sources.title: 3W Dataset 2.0.0: source origins
sources.attribution: Vaz Vargas, R. E., de Melo Junior, A. J., de Campos Lima, C. B. et al., Scientific Data 13, 949 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-07225-z.
sources.content: The 3W dataset includes real, simulated and hand-drawn time series. These are distinct data origins. Replaying a real historical record does not change its origin to simulated data and does not connect this dashboard to a live well.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH: association and causality
sources.attribution: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 3.1.3.6; accessed 2026-11-10. No NIST endorsement implied.
sources.license: NIST public-information reuse policy; no copyright marking on cited prose
sources.content: Observed association between variables alone does not establish a causal relationship. A shared or unobserved factor can produce association. In this dashboard, sensor summaries and a binary prediction support description of the recorded window, not a physical diagnosis.
